nodes.label: Graphify Context Layer
nodes.rationale: A persistent on-disk knowledge graph queried for context instead of re-reading the codebase each session; additive, so when missing every role falls back to normal reading and the harness never depends on it.

nodes.label: Graph Freshness Maintenance
nodes.rationale: A stale graph misleads, so keep it current: the post-commit hook re-runs deterministic free AST extraction on code, while semantic doc extraction costs tokens and runs on demand via /graphify --update.

nodes.label: graphify query Command
nodes.rationale: Roles prefer graphify query / path / explain over a cold read and quote the returned source_location when citing a fact.

nodes.label: graphify-out/graph.json Graph Data
nodes.rationale: Raw graph data in PROJECT_ROOT/graphify-out/ queried by graphify query, path, and explain; its presence/staleness gates the verifier advisory.

nodes.label: GRAPH_REPORT.md Audit
nodes.rationale: Plain-language audit of god nodes, communities, and surprising edges the leader reads to scope exploration and spot cross-module coupling before delegating.

nodes.label: HARNESS_WORKSPACE Resolution Order
nodes.rationale: Resolution precedence harness.config.json -> feature_list.json config -> .handyman/ -> legacy fallback keeps mutable state out of the repo root while staying discoverable.

nodes.label: Handyman Skill (agent work harness)
nodes.rationale: Core idea: the chat coordinates but the disk is the source of truth; every session has state, backlog, closure criteria and executable verification. Formerly named Foreman.

nodes.label: Local vs Global Install Modes
nodes.rationale: local keeps docs versioned next to code under .handyman/; global moves operational state to $HOME/HANDYMAN/<project> to keep the repo clean.

nodes.label: Anti Telefono Descompuesto Pattern
nodes.rationale: Long agent reports are written to backlog/ files and the chat only returns references, avoiding degradation of information between agents.

nodes.label: Obsidian Vault Integration
nodes.rationale: HARNESS_WORKSPACE opens directly as an Obsidian vault (frontmatter, #handyman/... tags, index.md MOC) without duplicating files.

nodes.norm_label: feature entity (id, name, status, acceptance, sprint, depends_on)

nodes.label: Agent Roles (leader / implementer / reviewer / explorer)
nodes.rationale: Roles communicate only through disk state and validate work with executable verification; each role has its own template, protocol, model default and least-privilege tool set.

nodes.label: HARNESS_WORKSPACE (Mutable State Root)
nodes.rationale: Mutable harness state (feature_list.json, progress/, backlog/, docs/) is isolated from the repo root so the code tree stays clean; resolution order is harness.config.json, then feature_list.json config, then PROJECT_ROOT/.handyman/, then legacy PROJECT_ROOT fallback. Local scope uses .handyman, global uses $HOME/HANDYMAN/<project_name>.

nodes.label: One Feature At A Time
nodes.rationale: Never mix unrelated feature work: at most one feature in_progress, lowest-id pending first. Keeps blast radius bounded and makes review and state coherence checkable (CHECKPOINTS C2).

nodes.label: Disk Is The Source Of Truth
nodes.rationale: All harness state lives on disk (feature_list.json, progress/current.md, progress/history.md) rather than in chat context, so sessions can be interrupted and resumed and agents cannot drift from unrecorded state.
nodes.norm_label: disk is the source of truth

nodes.label: Anti-Telefono-Descompuesto (Report Files Over Chat)
nodes.rationale: Subagents write full reports to $HARNESS_WORKSPACE/backlog/ (impl_, review_, explore_ files) and reply only with a file reference like 'done -> backlog/impl_cli_edit.md'. Prevents lossy relay of long diffs and findings through chat (the broken-telephone effect).

nodes.label: Executable Verification (Green Verifier Gate)
nodes.rationale: No feature is done until the verifier (normally ./init.sh) exits 0 with real tests. The agent does not claim it works; it demonstrates it. Guards against prose claiming success without evidence.

nodes.label: Untrusted Content Is Data, Not Instructions
nodes.rationale: Ingested files, tool output, code, web pages, backlog reports, and feature descriptions must never trigger actions; irreversible actions require explicit user confirmation. The leader, holding the widest tools, is the main injection target.
nodes.norm_label: untrusted content is data, not instructions

nodes.label: Least-Privilege Tools Per Role
nodes.rationale: Leader gets the widest tools (agent, web, browser); implementer and reviewer get no delegation or web; explorer is read-only without edit. Cheap fast models for implementer/reviewer, strong reasoning for the leader. Limits injection surface and cost.

nodes.label: feature_list.json (Central Feature State)
nodes.rationale: Single JSON file in HARNESS_WORKSPACE holding features with id, name, title, description, acceptance[], and status (pending/in_progress/done); mutated deterministically via node dist/feature.js rather than by hand.

nodes.label: init.sh Verifier
nodes.rationale: Executable gate run from PROJECT_ROOT: checks required harness files, validates state from HARNESS_WORKSPACE, runs tests. Exit 0 is the precondition for starting work and for marking any feature done.

nodes.label: backlog/ Report Convention (impl_/review_/explore_)
nodes.rationale: Per-task evidence files with role frontmatter written under $HARNESS_WORKSPACE/backlog/: impl_<feature>.md, review_<feature>.md, explore_<topic>.md. Generated deterministically by node dist/backlog.js and never overwritten.

nodes.label: Workspace As Obsidian Vault
nodes.rationale: The harness workspace doubles as an Obsidian vault: YAML frontmatter on every note, an index.md MOC, wiki links, and #handyman/... tags, making harness state browsable and queryable by humans.

nodes.label: Graphify Graph As Context Layer
nodes.rationale: Agents query the graphify knowledge graph (graphify query) before exploring code and keep it fresh with /graphify --update; explorers start from returned source_locations instead of scanning blindly.

nodes.label: Two-Stage Review (Spec Then Quality)
nodes.rationale: Stage 1 checks spec compliance against acceptance criteria and declared scope; a Stage 1 failure ends the review with CHANGES_REQUESTED without reaching Stage 2 (code quality), so spec drift is never buried under style feedback.

nodes.label: Feature Request Archetypes (Research vs Implementation)
nodes.rationale: Every request picks an archetype: [Research] leaves a plan in docs/, [Implementation] changes code plus tests. One request equals one feature; the green gate is always the last acceptance bullet; only name/title/description/acceptance become the feature_list.json entry.

nodes.label: Bootstrap Business Interview
nodes.rationale: docs/business.md must be filled during bootstrap by interviewing the user, never by inferring the domain from code, because the domain, stakeholders, and rules usually live only in the user's head. Bootstrap is incomplete until the file reflects real business context.

nodes.label: Role Files As Bridge Files
nodes.rationale: Agent/role files always live in platform-discoverable paths (.github/agents/ or .claude/agents/), never inside HARNESS_WORKSPACE, because the host only loads agents from those known paths; placing them in the workspace makes them undiscoverable and uninvocable.

nodes.label: Seven-Stage Feature Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Each stage (0-6 plus period close 7) has a deterministic guardian and leaves a dated artifact on disk; measures are derived from artifacts, never declared in the contract. Rule: a stage without its artifact did not happen.

nodes.label: Stability Check (preflight)
nodes.rationale: preflight.js orchestrates six controls (format, contract, version drift, config-role sync, discovery, worklist) but always exits 0: it reports stability rather than gating, because the blocking checks already live in the verifier's validate phase.

nodes.label: scaffold.sh (deterministic scaffold)
nodes.rationale: scaffold.sh is the canonical way to lay down the file set and writes harness.config.json in both scopes; snippets exist only for filling content, because re-creating the layout by hand is the main cause of cross-model drift.

nodes.label: feature-request.md Intake Form
nodes.rationale: Only name/title/description/acceptance become the feature_list.json entry; process-guidance sections are never stored keys, and the green gate is always the last acceptance bullet, mirroring how every closed feature ends its acceptance.

nodes.label: update_harness Updater CLI
nodes.source_location: Updating Models In An Existing Harness
nodes.rationale: Model names rotate; the updater edits the models/tools maps in harness.config.json and the frontmatter of every discovered role file in the same run so surfaces never drift apart.

nodes.label: Progressive Disclosure (skill loading)
nodes.source_location: How the platform discovers skills and MCPs
nodes.rationale: Only a skill's name and description sit in context; the body loads when the task matches. The description is therefore the trigger: a skill that describes itself poorly is simply not found.

nodes.label: discovery Block In harness.config.json
nodes.rationale: The block records names, never paths: names are portable intent that travels with the repo, while paths are machine-specific and resolved at query time. Deliver the path, do not store it. It is optional and global because skills/MCPs/agents are mostly cross-role.

nodes.label: tools_discovery CLI (list/find/check/declare)
nodes.rationale: The reproducible counterpart of the host's semantic discovery: skill roots scan local-first-then-global so a vendored skill shadows a global one; check gates on missing skills/agents but only NOTEs absent MCP servers because MCP availability is host-defined.

nodes.label: Deterministic vs Semantic Discovery Boundary
nodes.rationale: Handyman does not replace the platform's semantic discovery but wraps it in a declared, verifiable contract: the discovery block plus schemas plus the CLI are deterministic; the actual skill trigger and tool_search similarity stay semantic. The harness can declare and verify presence but cannot force a trigger.

nodes.label: Trigger Eval Set (evals/trigger-eval.json)
nodes.rationale: A balanced set of labeled queries with negatives written as near-misses: near-misses share vocabulary with the skill but ask for something else, which is what catches a description that over-triggers.

nodes.label: evals CLI (validate/measure)
nodes.rationale: validate is offline and gates; measure needs a runner and degrades to a NOTE with exit 0 when absent, so the stochastic half never blocks CI.

nodes.label: Deterministic Contract vs Stochastic Measurement
nodes.rationale: The eval-set contract is deterministic (same file, same answer) and safe to gate; the real trigger is model-dependent and drifts between runs, so it is measured, never asserted. Confusing the two makes the gate flaky, while leaning only on the size cap mistakes 'the description fits' for 'the description triggers'.

nodes.label: pass@k Completion Reliability
nodes.rationale: Derived from already-measured trigger rates as 1-(1-r)^k with no extra model calls; unlike a confusion matrix it exposes reliability under retry, the property that matters when the skill loads inside a long-running harness. Variance (mean +/- stddev over --runs) and a held-out split guard against noise and overfitting the wording.

nodes.label: Persistent Knowledge Graph (graphify-out/)
nodes.rationale: An additive context layer: agents query a persistent on-disk graph instead of re-reading the codebase each session; every edge is tagged EXTRACTED/INFERRED/AMBIGUOUS so agents can weigh trust. When the graph is missing every role falls back to normal reading, so the harness never depends on it.

nodes.label: Workspace As Obsidian Vault
nodes.source_location: Open The Workspace As A Vault
nodes.rationale: HARNESS_WORKSPACE doubles as an Obsidian vault without duplicating files: the same markdown agents read and write powers the visual workspace; Obsidian only adds visualization, search, backlinks, and tag navigation.

nodes.label: index.md Map Of Content (MOC)
nodes.rationale: Regenerated from live state with node dist/index_md.js; it links only files that exist and uses wikilinks for vault-internal targets so the verifier's link check stays green. Repo-root bridge files sit outside the vault and are referenced as plain paths.

nodes.label: Indirect Prompt Injection
nodes.rationale: Disk as source of truth means most context is text no one in the session authored; routing outside content into context is the point of the harness but also the injection path. Medium risk in the single-user supervised case, rising with team size, global installs, untrusted PRs, and web access.

nodes.label: ToolBox Live Observer (toolbox serve)
nodes.rationale: Pull, read-only, observe-don't-gate: a localhost-only web panel (disk -> fs.watch -> SSE -> browser) with hard 127.0.0.1 bind, Host-header check, GET-only, registry as read allowlist, and React text-only rendering so harness text never becomes markup. No foreign verifier runs unless --run-verifier is passed.

nodes.label: ToolBox Heartbeat (post_run closure event)
nodes.rationale: A drop-in post_run hook appending closure events to events.jsonl; feature done treats a failing post_run step as a warning, so a missing toolBox script never blocks a verified closure. timeline merges events with history, preferring history on collisions.

nodes.label: Client-Side BM25 Search (observer #/search)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately client-side retrieval: the RAG analysis concluded the harness corpus needs no server-side RAG pipeline — a BM25 index (MiniSearch) rebuilt from disk in milliseconds is immune to staleness, and agents keep using agentic search.

nodes.norm_label: explore report: toolbox a11y live regions

nodes.norm_label: explore report: workstation ui state (2nd pass)

nodes.label: Handyman Harness
nodes.rationale: Operational layer (files + roles + verification) installed around a repo so agent work is orderly, auditable and resumable: the chat coordinates, but disk is the source of truth. One feature at a time; nothing is done without a green executable verification.

nodes.label: HARNESS_WORKSPACE
nodes.rationale: Directory holding mutable harness state. Local: PROJECT_ROOT/.handyman; global: $HOME/HANDYMAN/<project>. Also functions as an Obsidian vault.

nodes.label: Verifier (init.sh)
nodes.rationale: Executable gate: orchestrates validate -> lint -> build -> test and gates closure; a feature can only become done with exit 0. Since feature 59, validate_harness runs inside the gate as a blocking phase.

nodes.label: Backlog Reports (anti-telefono-descompuesto)
nodes.rationale: Detail reports (impl_/review_/explore_*.md with YAML frontmatter) live on disk under backlog/; the chat only returns references, so long diffs and full context never degrade through chat relay.

nodes.label: Sprint (Period Partition)
nodes.rationale: Period label partitioning features; the sprint document is derived at close from artifacts already on disk, never maintained by hand in parallel.

nodes.label: feature_list.json State Machine
nodes.rationale: 4-state machine (pending/in_progress/done/blocked) validated against a JSON Schema with additionalProperties:false; at most one in_progress; deterministic stable writes so black-box tests do not break; never edited by hand - every mutation goes through a CLI (feature.js/sprint.js/backlog.js).

nodes.label: Sacred CLI Contract
nodes.rationale: Stable exit codes (0 ok, 1 error, 2 usage, 3 no ready work), messages to stderr, machine-readable stable stdout. No change may alter exit codes or output shape; subcommands and flags are protected by byte-parity black-box suites.

nodes.label: toolBox Observer
nodes.rationale: Read-only panel over the harness registry bound to 127.0.0.1: snapshots, signals, feature queue, timeline, BM25 corpus, LLM provider availability, graphify graph, SSE change feed. After feature 50 it is a single Next standalone process (toolbox_serve.ts deleted); the only disk-writing routes are POST /api/intake and, since feature 60, POST /api/feature.

nodes.label: @handyman/toolbox-core Package
nodes.rationale: HTTP-agnostic toolBox layer (LLM providers + relays draft/ask/summary, registry, resolveWorkspace, allowlisted state data layer with guards/corpus/md/tags/CSP) moved from handyman in feature 42; consumed via pnpm workspace:*; tsc -b project reference builds it first; handyman keeps re-export shims so historic dist entrypoints do not change.

nodes.label: Decision D-B: Relays Keep Separate Contracts
nodes.rationale: The three LLM relays (draft/summarize/ask) already share extracted choreography (lib/relay.ts body cap + SSE framing, lib/respond.ts 400s, core delta|result|error orchestration); what remains per route (~70 lines) declares how that relay genuinely differs (root/provider/model/context). A unified contract would need config flags as long as the code it replaces, and the 400 bodies are byte-fixed contract in tests - refactoring buys nothing and risks parity. New relays (32-35) do share a resolution prelude among themselves.
nodes.norm_label: decision d-b: relays keep separate contracts

nodes.label: Parity Oracle (black-box bash suites)
nodes.rationale: Black-box bash suites invoke each CLI and fix stdout/stderr/exit codes; they are runtime-agnostic, so a migrated script must keep its suite green pointed at the new entrypoint without editing assertions. This is what guarantees tests and orders are maintained across the Python->TS and Node->Next migrations (test_toolbox_serve.sh 48 cases, parameterizable via TOOLBOX_SERVE_CMD / TOOLBOX_BASE_URL).

nodes.label: Strangler Fig Migration Pattern
nodes.rationale: Migrate one script/route at a time: build the twin, verify byte-identical against the oracle suite, then delete the original; never big-bang. Applied first to Python+Bash->TypeScript (worktree per feature, oracle repointed without editing assertions) and then to toolbox_serve->Next.js (proxy fallback, routes stolen one by one).

nodes.label: LlmProvider Contract
nodes.rationale: {id, model, available(), draft(req, onDelta)} with LlmError taxonomy (unauthorized | insufficient_balance | provider_error); uses only web standards (fetch, AbortSignal, TextDecoder) so it is portable without changes; draft(req, onDelta) is the injectable test seam.

nodes.label: Declarative Provider Registry (PROVIDER_REGISTRY)
nodes.rationale: buildProviders was imperative code with env-var branches; a declarative registry table {id, adapter, baseUrl, envKey, defaultModel, quirks} makes adding a provider = adding an entry, without breaking the LlmProvider interface. Landed as feature 37 (toolbox_llm.ts PROVIDER_REGISTRY).

nodes.label: AI SDK 7 (deferred, decision D5)
nodes.rationale: createProviderRegistry/customProvider would standardize provider ids and test fakes, and is framework-agnostic; but major cadence (5->6->7 in ~12 months) demands exact pin + isolation in one module. Deferred (D5) because LlmProvider + PROVIDER_REGISTRY already suffice for unification; revisit after feature 50.

nodes.label: Next Runtime Singleton
nodes.rationale: SSE client set, fs.watch watchers, 250ms debounce, SummaryCache and providers assume one long-running process; in Next that means runtime nodejs (never edge), a globalThis module singleton that survives HMR in dev, and startup via instrumentation.ts register(). Landed as feature 43 (apps/web/lib/runtime.ts + instrumentation.ts).

nodes.label: Server Actions vs Route Handlers Split
nodes.rationale: Not everything can or should be a server action: actions are opaque React RPC not invocable with curl (the 48-case parity oracle would go blind), EventSource only does GET so /events can never be an action, actions cannot return raw streams with the byte-stable event: delta|result|error framing, and /graph/* //vendor/* need their own content-types. Server actions only where the pattern applies - the single real mutation (submitIntake) - over the same core function as the paritized POST /api/intake route handler; everything else stays route handlers in the same single app.
nodes.norm_label: server actions vs route handlers split

nodes.label: announce Module (ARIA Live Regions)
nodes.rationale: Reusable announce.polite/announce.assertive with a single queue + debounce. Assertive region = role=alert WITHOUT explicit aria-live (avoids double announcement in VoiceOver/iOS); polite = role=status + aria-live=polite. Announcing every SSE event degrades screen readers - same anti-noise principle as the LLM layer rule 'all LLM is pull or batch'. Fixes WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.3 Status Messages gap; the assertive region is the error surface the future LLM layer consumes. ariaNotify() rejected: not baseline (Firefox 150+ only).

nodes.label: Branch as Period Unit
nodes.rationale: The calendar sprint never triggered close (feature_archive.json had 0 entries, SP1-SP5 irregular over 3 weeks) while branch merges do happen; so the branch replaces the sprint as work unit: sprint open --label <branch> when opening a branch, sprint close as a merge step (fits pull-request-publish). sprint.ts code untouched; renaming sprint -> period/branch stays cosmetic future work.

nodes.label: handyman-mcp Server (F3)
nodes.rationale: Thin MCP wrapper over handyman/src/core (same code as the CLI, zero second source of truth). Value order: (1) contract moves from prose to code - feature_close rejects without green verifier, today that rule lives in markdown and depends on model obedience; (2) multi-repo hub - server reads $HOME/HANDYMAN/registry.json and tools take a project param, bridging to the panel-as-agent north star; (3) portability - any MCP client gets the verbs without the skill installed. Minimal surface: harness_list, preflight, feature_next, feature_close (gated), report_write, verify + resources.

nodes.label: Graphify Freshness Rule
nodes.rationale: Either automate graph freshness or drop the 'query graph first' rule - a written rule plus a dead graph is dishonest. Minimal proposal adopted: preflight advisory (context: NOTE) comparing graphify-out/graph.json mtime vs last commit, and /graphify --update as part of branch close (not every feature).

nodes.label: OKF v0.1 Spec (Open Knowledge Format)
nodes.rationale: .handyman is ~90% an OKF bundle already: the only MUST missing was type: in every .md frontmatter (plus frontmatter for 14 orphans) and markdown links without frontmatter in generated index.md. Conformance buys free interop (Google Cytoscape.js visualizer, Knowledge Catalog ingestion, any OKF consumer) with zero new lock-in; all current keys survive as tolerated extensions; wikilinks do not break conformance but stay invisible to OKF consumers.

nodes.label: esbuild Bundle (Variant A) for npm Package
nodes.rationale: Bundle toolbox-core into the package with esbuild instead of publishing two packages: self-contained 791.7 kB tarball (53 files, zero .env, zero workspace:*), smoke-tested outside the monorepo; variant B requires owning the @handyman npm scope or renaming imports, and means two publishes for a core whose only other consumer (apps/web) lives in the monorepo. CJS banner createRequire mandatory (ajv is CommonJS in ESM output); vis-network stays external as a normal dependency (resolved from node_modules to serve same-origin); publish as 3.0.0 so update_harness can distinguish incompatible states; files whitelist [dist, assets] keeps .env out; name handyman-harness was free on npm as of 2026-07-19.
nodes.norm_label: esbuild bundle (variant a) for npm package

nodes.label: Single handyman Bin Dispatcher
nodes.rationale: One bin `handyman <verb>` dispatching subcommands (~30-line dispatcher); the 12 dist entrypoints become internal detail; bash suites keep invoking node dist/*.js directly so the parity oracle is untouched (the dispatcher is additive). Level 1 of the three-level condensation: one command, same command for human and agent (npx handyman-harness in SKILL.md), then panel actions.

nodes.label: North Star: Panel as Agent
nodes.rationale: The declared north star: the panel as agent - a multi-repo hub to centralize ideas and execute from one place. Improvement ordering derives from this, not from ease. Bounded by the 'not an unattended runner' line in business.md: single human-triggered actions are in, an autonomous loop that picks the next feature and chains stages is a product change to be decided, not slipped in.

nodes.label: Workstation Panel (Python stdlib)
nodes.rationale: Localhost fleet panel on http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer: zero deps, zero build, all CSS/JS as Python f-strings baked once at startup. Security contract: bind 127.0.0.1, X-Workstation-Token on every POST, registry as write allowlist, DOM-safe rendering (textContent only, gate W011), mutations only via feature.py argv under MUTATION_LOCK. Hash-routed SPA (#/fleet, #/harness/<name>, #/timeline) with --hw- design tokens; 21 structural test cases W1-W21.

nodes.label: Design Tokens --hw-*
nodes.rationale: Single token set defined once in fleet.py _HTML_STYLE :root (color light/dark, 4 spacing steps, 3 type steps, system-ui font); the panel style only consumes and dark mode only reassigns tokens. Test W15 enforces zero hex outside --hw- lines across panel and fleet HTML.

nodes.label: Foreman (legacy name)
nodes.rationale: Handyman was previously known as Foreman; the new version keeps the same flow and adds native Obsidian integration over the same HARNESS_WORKSPACE.

nodes.label: Leader Role
nodes.rationale: Coordinates, resolves harness state, picks a feature and delegates; runs a strong reasoning model with the widest tool surface (agent, web, browser) and never edits product code.

nodes.label: Implementer Role
nodes.rationale: Implements exactly one feature with tests and disk evidence; defaults to a cheap fast model (fallback GLM-5.2) with no delegation or web tools.

nodes.label: Reviewer Role
nodes.rationale: Validates implementation against architecture, conventions, checkpoints and verification; cheap fast model (fallback GLM-5.2), no delegation or web, never edits code.

nodes.label: Explorer Role
nodes.rationale: Answers one narrow read-only question; cheapest model, read-only tools (no edit, no agent).

nodes.label: Local Install Mode (.handyman/)
nodes.rationale: Mutable state and operational docs live under a hidden .handyman/ so the repo root stays clean; only the docs layer is versioned (!.handyman/docs/) while operational state stays out of git.

nodes.label: Global Install Mode ($HOME/HANDYMAN)
nodes.rationale: State lives in $HOME/HANDYMAN/<project_name> with bridge files (AGENTS.md, CHECKPOINTS.md, init.sh, harness.config.json) left in the repo, separating source code from operational history.

nodes.label: toolBox Web Panel (@handyman/web)
nodes.rationale: Next.js panel observing registered harnesses (features, progress, backlog, search, optional LLM relays) on localhost:3210; self-contained because it embeds the toolBox observer in the same Node process by importing @handyman/toolbox-core directly, so no separate server is needed.

nodes.label: @handyman/toolbox-core
nodes.rationale: HTTP-agnostic data layer and LLM relays shared by the CLI toolchain and the web panel.

nodes.label: Registry As Read Allowlist
nodes.rationale: The registry ($HANDYMAN_ROOT/registry.json) doubles as a read allowlist: the panel only resolves files inside registered project roots and their workspaces.

nodes.label: LLM Relays (Claude, Z.AI, Ollama)
nodes.rationale: Optional relays (draft, triage, summaries) activated per provider by env vars (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, Z_AI_API_KEY, Ollama local, no key); the panel is fully functional without any keys.

nodes.label: PR Detail: toolBox Next.js And Honest Verbs
nodes.rationale: PR document for feat/llm-toolbox-tasks (features 41-63, plus registered 64-66): Next.js panel migration, toolbox-core extraction, honest verb contract, advisory noise reduction, open-source preparation, with evidence (init.sh 7 phases exit 0, all suites passed).
nodes.norm_label: pr detail: toolbox next.js and honest verbs

nodes.label: Observer Migration To Next.js
nodes.rationale: Full migration of the observer into apps/web (Next 16): 14 native API routes with byte parity against the retired Node observer, SSE via runtime singleton, live views via fs.watch -> SSE, and the panel's first write action (POST /api/feature) registering a feature without spawning processes.

nodes.label: Honest Verb Contract
nodes.rationale: 'done' writes the real verdict read from backlog/review_<name>.md (distinguishing NO REVIEW FILE from NO VERDICT); a single write path to feature_list.json (saveValidated); 'acceptance' on a done feature refuses unless an audited --force; init.sh runs validate_harness as a blocking phase; intake unified in one core function.

nodes.label: Open Source Preparation
nodes.rationale: Business decisions 2026-07-19: unified MIT license across the four workspace package.json (closing the Apache-2.0 contradiction), untracked 14 unlicensed third-party skills and machine-specific caches without deleting from disk, and registered the npm publication path (handyman-harness) as pending features 64-66.

nodes.label: handyman-harness (npm CLI)
nodes.rationale: CLI toolchain for the Handyman harness, run via npx handyman-harness. Verbs: backlog, evals, feature, index_md, metrics, preflight, sprint, toolbox, tools_discovery, update_harness, upgrade_harness, validate_harness. Typical loop: preflight, feature ready (exit 3 when drained), feature start, feature done.

nodes.label: Handyman Skill Manifest (SKILL.md)
nodes.rationale: Skill v3.1.0, user-invocable: the skill is the usage manifest while the deterministic tools live in the npm package handyman-harness; supersedes harness-subagents (Foreman).

nodes.label: HARNESS_WORKSPACE Resolution Order
nodes.rationale: Resolve harness.config.json first, then the feature_list.json config block, then PROJECT_ROOT/.handyman/, then the legacy PROJECT_ROOT fallback.

nodes.label: Skill-Toolchain Shared Versioning
nodes.rationale: metadata.version equals the published package.json, enforced at pack time; the pinned major (@3) delivers minors without skill edits; npx handyman-harness@3 --version reports the resolved toolchain.

nodes.label: Graphify Graph Integration
nodes.rationale: Query the graphify knowledge graph before exploring code and keep it fresh with /graphify --update; explorers start from returned source_locations instead of scanning blindly.

nodes.label: Explore Report Template
nodes.rationale: Template for backlog/explore_<topic>.md: one narrow question, findings, source locations for the leader to start from, open questions; frontmatter topic/role: explorer/updated/tags.

nodes.label: Implementation Log Template
nodes.rationale: Template for backlog/impl_<feature>.md: files changed, design notes, verifier test output; frontmatter feature/status: implemented/role: implementer/updated/tags.

nodes.label: Review Log Template
nodes.rationale: Template for backlog/review_<feature>.md: verdict APPROVED or CHANGES_REQUESTED, two-stage checklist, required changes; frontmatter feature/status/role: reviewer/updated/tags.

nodes.label: Architecture Doc Template
nodes.rationale: Defines what good work means in the repo (layers, dependency policy, explicit errors, data and IO policy, data flow, what not to do); reviewers evaluate code against it.

nodes.label: Mandatory Business Interview
nodes.rationale: Fill docs/business.md during bootstrap by interviewing the user, never by inferring from code: the domain, stakeholders and rules usually live only in the user's head; bootstrap is not complete until the file reflects real business context instead of the template.

nodes.label: Conventions Doc Template
nodes.rationale: Language/runtime, tests, error handling and comments conventions; prefer clear names, comment only non-obvious reasoning.

nodes.label: Verification Doc Template
nodes.rationale: The agent does not claim it works; it demonstrates it. Required command ./init.sh; test levels unit/integration/smoke. Anti-patterns: marking done with red tests, tests that only assert no exception, mocking the core behavior that should be proven.

nodes.label: Index MOC Template
nodes.rationale: Obsidian map-of-content linking feature_list.json, feature-request.md, docs, progress and backlog reports; bridge files AGENTS.md and CHECKPOINTS.md live in PROJECT_ROOT outside the vault in both install modes.

nodes.label: Current Session Template
nodes.rationale: Reset when a session closes and its summary moves to history; keeps active feature, start, agent, a 3-5 bullet plan, live log and the next step so an interrupted session can resume.

nodes.label: Session History Template
nodes.rationale: Append-only; each entry records branch (also the period label), tools, evidence (impl report plus the uppercased status of review_<feature>.md, or NO REVIEW FILE / NO VERDICT) and verification; the narrative lives in the backlog reports the Evidence line points at, never duplicated here.

nodes.label: Actor Attribution (actor: frontmatter)
nodes.rationale: Optional, never-blocking actor: line names who implemented and who reviewed; when the same actor appears on both reports for a feature the verifier prints a NOTE that the review was not independent - a collapsed-roles run is visible in the record, not hidden.

nodes.label: Sprint Document Template
nodes.rationale: Closed work period document: every section except manual Achievements and Lessons is derived at close time from feature_list.json, progress/history.md and backlog/ frontmatter by npx handyman-harness@3 sprint close; regenerate rather than hand-edit.

nodes.label: Harness Anatomy
nodes.rationale: A harness repo is a normal software project plus an explicit operating system for agents; the harness makes work auditable, repeatable and reviewable.

nodes.label: PROJECT_ROOT
nodes.rationale: The repo where product code, tests, verifier scripts and stable agent entrypoints live.

nodes.label: Obsidian Frontmatter And Tag Namespace
nodes.rationale: Mutable markdown carries YAML frontmatter (feature, status, role, updated, tags) and the #handyman/... namespace (feature/role/review/session/history/docs/blocked/moc) so Obsidian can index harness state; .obsidian/ stays out of version control.

nodes.label: Shared Observation Shape
nodes.rationale: Support scripts converge on a shared observation shape: the last stdout line is 'status: ok|warn|error' preceded by a 'next:' hint when one applies (JSON payload in --json modes), so callers and loop runners read that tail instead of parsing prose.

nodes.label: Contract vs Resolution (Names Travel, Paths Do Not)
nodes.rationale: The contract declares portable names; paths resolve per user/machine/scope at query time and are never persisted. Deliver the path, do not store it: a stored absolute path breaks portability the moment the repo moves; a resolved path is always correct for the environment that asked.
nodes.norm_label: contract vs resolution (names travel, paths do not)

nodes.label: trigger-eval.json Eval Set
nodes.rationale: Balanced labeled queries (equal positives/negatives, multiple languages). Negatives are near-misses sharing vocabulary with the skill but asking for something else: they are the valuable negatives because they catch an over-triggering description.

nodes.label: Held-Out Split and Variance
nodes.rationale: A model trigger is noisy so a single run is not a measurement: each query runs N times producing a rate with mean and stddev. When tuning the description, judge candidates on a held-out split they were not tuned on; tuning and scoring on the same queries overfits wording to those phrases instead of the intent.

nodes.label: Example: Run One Feature
nodes.rationale: Shows form-first intake, feature add with only contract keys, delegation where subagents return one reference line (done -> backlog/impl_*.md, APPROVED -> backlog/review_*.md) instead of pasting reports into chat, and closure only after approval plus green verifier.

nodes.label: Per-Role Models
nodes.rationale: Spend reasoning budget where decisions are made: leader gets the strongest reasoning model; implementer/reviewer do bounded well-specified work and run frequently so a cheaper model keeps the loop affordable; explorer gets the cheapest fast model. The optional models map in harness.config.json centralizes assignment so role files stay generic.

nodes.label: GLM-5.2 Placeholder Default
nodes.rationale: Placeholder identifier for the cheap-role default; replace with the exact name or alias the host exposes (e.g. sonnet in Claude Code) and pick the closest Sonnet-class model when the exact version is not listed.

nodes.label: HARNESS_WORKSPACE as Obsidian Vault
nodes.rationale: The same markdown agents read and write powers the visual workspace without duplicating files; Obsidian only adds visualization, search, backlinks, and tag navigation. Wikilinks for vault-internal cross-references, markdown links for non-Obsidian readers; repo-root bridge files (AGENTS.md, CHECKPOINTS.md) live outside the vault in both modes.

nodes.label: Harness Gitignore Policy
nodes.rationale: Ignore operational state (.handyman/*) but keep .handyman/docs/ versioned: the conceptual docs layer (business, architecture, conventions, verification) is the part worth versioning with the project. Also ignore .obsidian/ and .trash/. In global installs mutable state lives outside the repo entirely.

nodes.label: Template Asset Library (assets/)
nodes.rationale: Full template bodies live as standalone files under assets/ so they can be copied directly. scaffold.sh is the canonical way to lay down the file set; the snippets exist for filling content and per-file customization. Re-creating the layout by hand is the main cause of cross-model drift (e.g. harness.config.json appearing in one bootstrap and not another).

nodes.label: ToolBox (Multi-Harness Observation)
nodes.rationale: Philosophy: pull, read-only, observe-don't-gate (status/health never mutate and exit 0 by default; gating opt-in via health --strict); disk is the source of truth (registry stores only project_root + date, everything else read live so no mirrored state drifts); drift tolerant (missing fields degrade to null/NOTE, unreadable roots become an UNREADABLE signal, not a crash); no foreign verifier runs without the explicit --run-verifier opt-in. TypeScript port of the legacy fleet layer.

nodes.label: ToolBox LLM Layer
nodes.rationale: One LlmProvider interface with two adapters parameterized by baseUrl: Anthropic Messages (Claude; Z.ai GLM Coding Plan verified at api.z.ai/api/anthropic) and OpenAI-compatible (Z.ai paas mode; Ollama availability-probed); copilot is a declared future id. Keys load from the launch directory's .env (existing env wins, values never logged) and never reach the browser: /api/providers returns only id, available, model.

nodes.label: Intake-Draft Relay (POST /api/draft)
nodes.rationale: Builds the intake prompt from the stable cacheable template (CORE/OPTIONAL shape, two archetypes, green-gate-as-last-bullet, feature add contract) plus volatile target-harness context (feature queue, top-k BM25 duplicate candidates, discovery skills/agents, tagged files), streams the draft over SSE (delta/result/error events). It never writes disk: the draft always passes through the human before any destination, and seeding feature_list.json stays with the leader via feature add.

nodes.label: Intake Submit (POST /api/intake)
nodes.rationale: The observer's only disk write: persists the reviewed draft to one allowlisted file (feature-request.md) inside a registered workspace, appends tagged files as an HTML comment footer, refuses invalid/empty payloads with 4xx, and never spawns a process; the feature still enters feature_list.json via feature add.

nodes.label: Unified Next Panel (apps/web)
nodes.rationale: The observer frontend is the unified Next panel served as a standalone build by toolbox serve; the legacy assets/toolbox_panel.js was retired.

nodes.label: Observer UI Features (Plans A-E)
nodes.rationale: Intentionally hand-rolled, no chart/markdown/theme library: (A) KPI strip + inline SVG throughput sparkline from metrics.collect(); (B) anti-flash theme toggle via inline head script + data-theme tokens; (C) safe markdown with marked + DOMPurify treating agent output as untrusted, CSP as second defense; (D) two persistent aria-live regions with debounced summaries, reduced-motion support, actionable empty states; (E) native <dialog> command palette ranked by the existing MiniSearch index with global shortcuts guarded by an event.target check.

nodes.label: Preflight Stability Check
nodes.rationale: Read-only review before feature work orchestrating six controls: format (validate_harness), feature-list schema contract, version drift (upgrade_harness --check), config-to-role-file sync (update_harness --check, config is source of truth), discovery check, and the ready worklist. Always exits 0 — it reports stability, does not gate; blocking checks already live in the verifier's validate phase.

nodes.label: post_run Hooks
nodes.rationale: Optional shell commands in harness.config.json that run automatically after a verified close, always with exit 0: a failing custom step only WARNs and never reverts a verified close. Typical uses: regenerate index.md, refresh a context graph, re-measure a description trigger.

nodes.label: feature CLI (add/start/log/next/done/ready/block)
nodes.rationale: Deterministic state mutations: add writes only contract keys (hand-editing feature_list.json is how out-of-contract keys such as date fields creep in); start records the branch; log/next keep session format and updated stamp consistent; done refuses to close without a green verifier and writes the standard history entry; ready lists pending features with satisfied depends_on (exit 3 = drained); block/unblock manage the blocked state.

nodes.label: allowBuilds Policy
nodes.rationale: sharp is declined: it is next/image's optional native optimizer and unused (zero pages, no next/image in the scaffold), so its postinstall build is skipped. esbuild is approved: its postinstall validates the platform binary arriving via optionalDependencies, so the npm-pack staging build (feature 64) runs the same locally and in CI.
